transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

22E on a Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU normally means a refrigerator-compartment evaporator fan fault — the fan behind the rear panel in the fridge section is not turning or the control board is not receiving its speed signal.

That fits your symptom: without that fan, cold air is not circulated around the fridge side, so it becomes warmer than it should.

### Things you can safely try

1. Check that the internal air vents are not blocked
• Move food away from the rear wall and vents.
• Make sure the fridge door is closing fully and the door seal is clean.

2. Power-reset it
• Switch the appliance off at the wall / unplug it for about 5–10 minutes, then restart it.
• This may clear a temporary electronic fault, but it will not cure a failed or ice-bound fan.

3. Fully defrost it if there is any sign of ice
   A common cause is ice building up behind the fridge’s internal rear cover and physically jamming the fan.
• Move food to another fridge/cool box if possible.
• Switch off and unplug the appliance.
• Leave both doors open for at least 24 hours; 36–48 hours is better if there is heavy hidden ice.
• Put towels down for meltwater.
• Do not chip ice with a knife or use a high-heat device on plastic panels.
• Restart it and allow up to 24 hours for temperatures to stabilise.

If the error disappears and cooling returns after a proper defrost, ice was likely stopping the fan. If it returns days or weeks later, there may be an underlying defrost-system issue as well.

### When it needs an engineer

If 22E returns straight away, or the fridge remains warm after defrosting, the likely causes are:

• failed fridge evaporator fan motor;
• damaged fan wiring/connector;
• ice recurrence caused by a defrost heater, sensor or drainage problem;
• less commonly, a control-board fault.

Those require access behind the internal rear panel and are generally a Samsung service/repair job.

### Food safety

Until it is cooling properly, try to keep the fridge compartment at 5 °C or below. If chilled food has been above that for a prolonged period, especially meat, fish, dairy or cooked leftovers, follow local food-safety guidance and err on the side of caution.

In short: 22E = fridge evaporator fan problem. A full defrost is the main DIY fix worth trying; if the code persists, arrange service for the fan/defrost system.

I tried the power reset at the wall for a few minutes, but 22E came back within a few hours. There's no burning smell and nothing has tripped. Should I go ahead with the full defrost, or is this a job for an engineer?

Yes — assuming the appliance is out of warranty and you can keep the food safely chilled elsewhere, a full manual defrost is a sensible next step before calling an engineer.

A brief power reset will not clear ice that may be jamming the fridge evaporator fan. With a 22E error that returns after a few hours, the two most likely possibilities are:

1. Ice behind the internal rear panel is stopping the fridge evaporator fan, or
2. The fan motor / wiring has failed.

A proper defrost helps distinguish between them.

### Do the full defrost

• Switch the fridge-freezer off at the socket and unplug it.
• Empty it as far as possible; protect refrigerated/frozen food in another appliance or cool boxes with ice packs.
• Leave both doors open for 24 hours minimum. Ideally allow 36–48 hours if you can, because ice behind the internal fridge rear cover can take much longer to melt than visible frost.
• Put towels around the base for water.
• Do not prise at panels or ice with sharp tools, and do not use a heat gun/hairdryer close to plastic parts.

Then restart it, set normal temperatures, and allow roughly 12–24 hours for it to settle.

### What the result means

• 22E clears and the fridge cools normally: it was probably ice stopping the fan. Keep an eye on it.
• 22E returns immediately or within a day, and the fridge remains warm: arrange an engineer. The evaporator fan motor, its wiring, or the control board is likely faulty.
• It works after defrosting but 22E returns after days/weeks: it may have a defrost-system problem — such as a defrost heater, sensor, drain issue, or seal/air-leak issue — causing ice to build up again. That is also an engineer repair.

No burning smell and no tripped electrics is reassuring, but it does not rule out a fan motor or sensor fault; these are usually low-power electrical parts and do not normally trip a circuit.

If the appliance is still within Samsung warranty or an extended retailer warranty, contact them before dismantling any internal panels. A full door-open defrost is fine, but I would not remove the rear internal cover unless you are confident working on appliances.
